questions.q: Where must a GitHub Actions workflow file live for GitHub to recognize it automatically?
options: In a private GitHub Settings page only admins can edit
Inside .github/workflows/ at the root of the repository — no separate registration step is needed
It must be uploaded through a separate CI service, not committed to the repo
Anywhere in the repository, as long as it ends in .yml
questions.explain: GitHub automatically scans the exact .github/workflows/ folder; committing a file there is the entire setup.

questions.q: What are the three core pieces that make up a GitHub Actions workflow file?
options: header, body, footer
source, target, and destination
on (the trigger), jobs (units of work), and steps (ordered commands inside a job)
install, build, and ship
questions.explain: A workflow defines what event triggers it (on), one or more jobs that each run on their own fresh VM, and the ordered steps within each job.

questions.q: What does the `uses: actions/checkout@v4` step do, and why is it so common?
options: It deletes the repository from the runner
It checks out a specific employee's work schedule
It is only used for deployment workflows, never for testing
It clones the repository onto the runner, which otherwise starts with no code on it at all
questions.explain: A fresh runner VM has no code by default; actions/checkout is the standard reusable action that clones the repository so later steps have something to work with.

questions.q: Where can you find every workflow run for a repository, across every workflow file?
options: The repository's Issues tab
Only in email notifications, nowhere on the site itself
A separate GitHub account you must create
The repository's Actions tab
questions.explain: The Actions tab lists every run, past and present, for every workflow file defined in the repository.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the actual value of expanding a job's step-level logs?
options: It shows which specific step failed and its output, rather than just a vague job-level red X
It lets you edit the workflow file directly from the log view
It automatically fixes any failing step
It has no practical use beyond curiosity
questions.explain: Step-level logs are where real debugging happens — they pinpoint exactly which step failed and show its output, instead of just an overall pass/fail status.
